items.q: A solution is a ____ mixture.
The number of components in a binary solution is
items.x: Binary = one solute + one solvent.

items.q: Which of the following is the universal solvent?
items.x: Water dissolves more substances than any other solvent.

items.q: A solution in which no more solute can be dissolved in a definite amount of solvent at a given temperature is called
Identify the non-aqueous solution.
items.x: The solvent is CS₂, not water.

items.q: When pressure is increased at constant temperature, the solubility of gases in liquids
items.x: Henry's law: solubility of a gas is proportional to its pressure.

items.q: Solubility of NaCl in 100 mL water is 36 g. If 25 g of salt is dissolved in 100 mL of water, how much more salt is required for saturation?
A 25% alcohol solution means
o: 25 mL alcohol in 100 mL of water
25 mL alcohol in 25 mL of water
25 mL alcohol in 75 mL of water
75 mL alcohol in 25 mL of water
items.x: 25 mL alcohol in 100 mL of solution, i.e. 25 mL alcohol + 75 mL water.

items.q: Deliquescence is due to
Which of the following is hygroscopic in nature?
items.x: Silica gel absorbs moisture without dissolving; ferric chloride is deliquescent.

items.q: The component present in lesser amount in a solution is called the ____.
items.a: solute

items.q: An example of a liquid-in-solid type solution is ____.
items.a: mercury in sodium (sodium amalgam)

items.q: Solubility is the amount of solute dissolved in ____ g of solvent.
Polar compounds are soluble in ____ solvents.
items.a: polar

items.q: Volume percentage decreases with increase in temperature because ____.
items.a: the liquid expands on heating, so the volume of the solution increases

items.q: Match the following.
Solutions which contain three components are called binary solutions.
items.x: Solutions with two components are binary; three components make a ternary solution.

items.q: In a solution, the component which is present in lesser amount is called the solvent.
items.x: The component in lesser amount is the solute; the one in larger amount is the solvent.

items.q: Sodium chloride dissolved in water forms a non-aqueous solution.
items.x: It forms an aqueous solution, because water is the solvent.

items.q: The molecular formula of green vitriol is MgSO₄·7H₂O.
items.x: Green vitriol is FeSO₄·7H₂O; MgSO₄·7H₂O is Epsom salt.

items.q: When silica gel is kept open, it absorbs moisture from the air because it is hygroscopic in nature.
Define the term solution.
items.a: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances (solute and solvent).

items.q: What is meant by a binary solution?
items.a: A solution made of only two components, one solute and one solvent, e.g. salt in water.

items.q: Give an example each of (i) gas in liquid (ii) solid in liquid (iii) solid in solid (iv) gas in gas.
items.a: (i) CO₂ in water (soda water) (ii) sugar or salt in water (iii) alloys such as brass (zinc in copper) (iv) air (oxygen in nitrogen).

items.q: What are aqueous and non-aqueous solutions? Give an example.
items.a: Aqueous: water is the solvent, e.g. sodium chloride in water. Non-aqueous: a solvent other than water, e.g. sulphur in carbon disulphide.

items.q: Define volume percentage.
items.a: The volume of solute in mL present in 100 mL of solution. Volume % = volume of solute ÷ volume of solution × 100.

items.q: Aquatic animals live more in cold regions. Why?
items.a: The solubility of oxygen in water is higher at low temperature, so cold water holds more dissolved oxygen.

items.q: Define hydrated salt.
items.a: A salt whose crystals contain a fixed number of water molecules (water of crystallisation), e.g. CuSO₄·5H₂O.

items.q: A hot saturated solution of copper sulphate forms crystals as it cools. Why?
items.a: Solubility of copper sulphate decreases as the temperature falls, so the extra solute that can no longer stay dissolved separates as crystals.

items.q: Classify into deliquescent and hygroscopic: conc. sulphuric acid, copper sulphate pentahydrate, silica gel, calcium chloride and gypsum salt.
items.a: Deliquescent: calcium chloride. Hygroscopic: conc. sulphuric acid, silica gel. Copper sulphate pentahydrate and gypsum are hydrated salts (they already contain water of crystallisation); some guides list them as hygroscopic.

items.q: Write notes on (i) saturated solution (ii) unsaturated solution.
items.a: (i) Saturated: a solution in which no more solute can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a given temperature, e.g. 36 g of NaCl in 100 g of water at 25 °C. (ii) Unsaturated: a solution that contains less solute than it can hold, so more solute can still dissolve, e.g. 10 g of NaCl in 100 g of water at 25 °C.

items.q: Write notes on the various factors affecting solubility.
items.a: 1) Nature of solute and solvent: 'like dissolves like', so polar solutes dissolve in polar solvents (NaCl in water) and non-polar in non-polar (grease in petrol). 2) Temperature: for most solids, solubility increases with temperature (endothermic dissolution, e.g. KNO₃); it decreases when dissolution is exothermic (e.g. CaO). Solubility of gases in liquids decreases with temperature. 3) Pressure: affects only gases; by Henry's law the solubility of a gas in a liquid increases with pressure (soda bottles).

items.q: (a) What happens when MgSO₄·7H₂O is heated? Write the equation. (b) Define solubility.
items.a: (a) It loses its seven molecules of water of crystallisation and becomes anhydrous magnesium sulphate: MgSO₄·7H₂O → MgSO₄ + 7H₂O. (b) Solubility is the number of grams of solute needed to saturate 100 g of solvent at a given temperature.

items.q: In what way do hygroscopic substances differ from deliquescent substances?
items.a: Hygroscopic substances absorb moisture from air but do not dissolve in it, and keep their physical state (e.g. conc. H₂SO₄, silica gel, CaO). Deliquescent substances absorb so much moisture that they dissolve in it and turn into a solution (e.g. NaOH, CaCl₂, FeCl₃).

items.q: A solution is prepared by dissolving 45 g of sugar in 180 g of water. Calculate the mass percentage of solute.
3.5 litres of ethanol is present in 15 litres of aqueous solution of ethanol. Calculate the volume percent of ethanol.
Vinu dissolves 50 g of sugar in 250 mL of hot water; Sarath dissolves 50 g of the same sugar in 250 mL of cold water. Who gets faster dissolution, and why?
items.a: Vinu. Sugar dissolves faster in hot water because solubility and the speed of the particles increase with temperature.

items.q: 'A' is a blue crystalline salt. On heating it loses its blue colour to give 'B'. When water is added, 'B' gives back 'A'. Identify A and B and write the equation.
items.a: A = copper sulphate pentahydrate CuSO₄·5H₂O (blue vitriol); B = anhydrous copper sulphate CuSO₄ (white). CuSO₄·5H₂O ⇌ CuSO₄ + 5H₂O (heat forward, add water back).

items.q: Will cool drinks give more fizz at the top of the hills or at the foot? Explain.
items.a: At the top of the hills. Atmospheric pressure is lower there, so less CO₂ stays dissolved (Henry's law) and the gas escapes rapidly when the bottle is opened.

items.q: Salt in water and sand in water differ because:
o: Salt dissolves to form a homogeneous mixture, sand can be separated by filtration
items.x: Salt dissolves forming a homogeneous mixture (solution); sand does not dissolve and can be filtered.

items.q: Which of the following is cited in the chapter as a naturally existing solution?
items.x: Sea water (a mixture of many dissolved salts) and air are given as naturally existing solutions.

items.q: Which liquids of the human body are described as solutions?
items.x: Most body liquids including blood, lymph and urine are solutions.

items.q: In a solution, the component present in the larger amount (by weight) is called:
items.x: The solvent is the component in larger amount and acts as the dissolving medium.

items.q: The process of uniform distribution of solute into solvent is called:
items.x: Uniform distribution of solute into solvent is called dissolution.

items.q: A solution of salt and sugar in water is an example of a:
items.x: Two solutes in one solvent make three components, a ternary solution.

items.q: Which factor primarily determines the characteristics of a binary solution?
items.x: The solvent constitutes the major part, so its physical state is the primary factor.

items.q: Match the solution with its type: A. Copper in gold  B. Sodium amalgam  C. Soda water  D. Cloud with 1. Liquid in gas  2. Gas in liquid  3. Liquid in solid  4. Solid in solid
items.x: Table 9.1: copper in gold (alloy) is solid in solid, mercury with sodium is liquid in solid, soda water gas in liquid, cloud liquid in gas.

items.q: Why is water called the 'universal solvent'?
o: Most substances are soluble in it
items.x: Most substances are soluble in water, so it is called the universal solvent.

items.q: Which of the following is a non-aqueous solution?
items.x: Sulphur in carbon disulphide and iodine in carbon tetrachloride are non-aqueous solutions.

items.q: At 25 °C, 40 g of sodium chloride in 100 g of water forms a:
items.x: 36 g saturates 100 g water at 25 °C, so 40 g is more than saturation: supersaturated.

items.q: Which statement about supersaturated solutions is correct?
o: They are unstable and the solute reappears as crystals when disturbed
They contain less solute than a saturated solution
They cannot be made by changing temperature
items.x: Supersaturated solutions are unstable; the solute crystallizes when the solution is disturbed.

items.q: Classifying solutions as 'dilute' and 'concentrated' is:
items.x: Dilute and concentrated is a qualitative representation and does not imply the quantity of solute.

items.q: The solubility of NaCl in water at 25 °C is:
items.x: 36 g of NaCl dissolves in 100 g water to form a saturated solution at 25 °C.

items.q: Solubility of NaCl is 36 g per 100 g water. If 25 g is already dissolved in 100 g water, how much more is needed for saturation?
items.x: 36 − 25 = 11 g more salt is required to saturate the solution.

items.q: The phrase 'like dissolves like' means:
o: Dissolving occurs when solute and solvent are similar, e.g. polar in polar
items.x: Polar compounds like common salt dissolve in polar water; non-polar compounds like fat dissolve in non-polar ether.

items.q: Consider: 1. In an endothermic process, solubility increases with temperature. 2. In an exothermic process, solubility decreases with temperature. Which is/are correct?
items.x: The chapter states both: endothermic dissolution increases and exothermic decreases with rising temperature.

items.q: Why do bubbles appear when water is heated?
o: The solubility of dissolved oxygen decreases with rising temperature
items.x: Solubility of gases in liquids decreases with temperature, so dissolved oxygen escapes as bubbles.

items.q: Aquatic animals live more in cold regions because:
o: Cold water contains more dissolved oxygen
items.x: Solubility of oxygen in water is higher at low temperatures.

items.q: Pressure has a noticeable effect on solubility only for:
items.x: The effect of pressure is observed only in the case of a gas dissolving in a liquid.

items.q: Henry's law states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is:
o: Directly proportional to the pressure of the gas over the solution
items.x: Henry's law: solubility of a gas is directly proportional to its pressure over the solution at a definite temperature.

items.q: Formalin is an aqueous solution of:
items.x: The chapter names formalin as an aqueous solution of formaldehyde.

items.q: A 5 % sugar solution by mass means:
items.x: 5 g of sugar in 95 g of water gives 100 g of solution.

items.q: Which concentration term is independent of temperature?
items.x: Mass percentage (w/w) is independent of temperature; volume percentage decreases as liquids expand.

items.q: A 25 % alcohol solution (v/v) means:
items.x: Volume percentage is volume of solute per volume of solution; 25 ml alcohol + 75 ml water = 100 ml solution.

items.q: In commercial products, the concentration of ointments, antacids and soaps is usually expressed as:
items.x: Syrups, mouthwash and disinfectants use v/v; ointments, antacids and soaps use w/w.

items.q: A solution has 35 ml of methanol and 65 ml of water. Its volume percentage is:
The number of water molecules in a crystalline substance is called:
items.x: The number of water molecules found in the crystalline substance is the water of crystallization.

items.q: When blue copper sulphate crystals are gently heated they:
o: Lose five water molecules and become colourless anhydrous copper sulphate
items.x: CuSO4.5H2O loses its 5 water molecules and becomes colourless; adding water restores the blue colour.

items.q: Match the common names with formulas: A. Blue vitriol  B. Epsom salt  C. Gypsum  D. Green vitriol with 1. CaSO4.2H2O  2. FeSO4.7H2O  3. CuSO4.5H2O  4. MgSO4.7H2O
items.x: Table 9.3: blue vitriol CuSO4.5H2O, Epsom salt MgSO4.7H2O, gypsum CaSO4.2H2O, green vitriol FeSO4.7H2O.

items.q: White vitriol is:
items.x: White vitriol is zinc sulphate heptahydrate, ZnSO4.7H2O.

items.q: The water of crystallization of Epsom salt is:
items.x: Magnesium sulphate heptahydrate (MgSO4.7H2O) has 7 water molecules.

items.q: Which of the following is a hygroscopic substance used as a drying agent?
items.x: Conc. H2SO4, P2O5, quick lime and silica gel are hygroscopic; NaOH, KOH and FeCl3 are deliquescent.

items.q: Deliquescence is maximum when:
o: Temperature is low and atmosphere is humid
Temperature is high and air is dry
Temperature is high and atmosphere is humid
items.x: Deliquescence is maximum when the temperature is low and the atmosphere is humid.

items.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes deliquescent from hygroscopic substances?
o: Deliquescent substances absorb moisture and dissolve; hygroscopic substances absorb moisture without dissolving
Hygroscopic substances dissolve in absorbed water
items.x: Deliquescent substances (crystalline solids) change state and dissolve; hygroscopic ones do not change state.

items.q: 1.5 g of a solute saturates 15 g of water at 298 K. Its solubility is:
items.x: Solubility = 1.5 / 15 × 100 = 10 g.

items.q: The solubility of sodium nitrate is 114 g at 50 °C and 96 g at 30 °C. How much salt is thrown out when a saturated solution with 50 g of water is cooled from 50 °C to 30 °C?
items.x: At 50 °C, 50 g water holds 57 g; at 30 °C it holds 48 g; 57 − 48 = 9 g is thrown out.

items.q: The mass percentage of a solution made by dissolving 25 g of sugar in 100 g of water is:
How much urea must be dissolved to make 500 g of a 10 % w/w aqueous solution?
items.x: Mass of urea = 10 × 500 / 100 = 50 g.

items.q: Will a cool drink give more fizz at the top of a hill or at its foot, and why?
o: At the foot, because pressure is lower there
At the top, because the lower air pressure lets dissolved CO2 escape faster
At the top, because temperature is higher
items.x: Gas solubility rises with pressure (Henry's law); at the lower pressure on a hilltop, CO2 comes out more readily.
